chunks: And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥajjāj narrated from Abī Ibrāhīm عليه السلام:
Concerning a man who performed saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah in eight circuits, he said: “If it was by mistake, he should discard one and count seven.”
And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, he said:

key_terms.أَشْوَاطٍ: circuits or laps in the ritual movement
key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Ṣafā, one of the two stations of saʿy
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the other station of saʿy
key_terms.ثَمَانِيَةَ: eight, referring here to the number of circuits completed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone performs eight circuits of saʿy between Ṣafā and Marwah by mistake?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling for someone who performs eight circuits of saʿy between al-Ṣafā and al-Marwah instead of seven. One report states that if this happened by mistake, one circuit is disregarded and the saʿy is counted as seven, while another report states that six more circuits are added.
